17w5f7.625: An irregular double-plan castle with a polygonal main façade reached by a large stone ramp; the cobbled courtyard leads to a three-arched loggia with Ghibelline blackbirds on the noble floor. Some scholars date to the year 1000 the western tower with a polygonal sloping base; the family De Sterlich-Aliprandi, present from the XV-XVI century, owned it until the mid-Twentieth century, when the building had already lost its military function. With the houses-walls, it delimits a ring space around the hill; the restoration was completed in 1993 and many rooms conserve vaults, arches and stone pillars.
g136y8.39: The crenellated loggia and the stone ramp.
8k1sew.388: Permanent collection of contemporary Abruzzo artists in the rooms of the castle, with works by Franco Summa, Michele Cascella, Nino Caffè and Remo Brindisi, and temporary exhibitions with activities including visual arts, literature, theater, cinema, music and new technologies. Hours (MiC card): Saturday 10-12:30, Sunday 16-18:30; other days and guided tours by telephone (349 6096186).

13qu9qm.301: A small village on the fishing side of Majella, linked to Pietro da Morrone, the future Celestine V: in its territory there are the Celestinian hermitages of Santo Spirito in Majella, the largest and most famous of the mountains, and San Bartolomeo in Legio, dug in the rock of the Vallone di Santo Spirito.
16la7v5.716: The greatest and best known of the Majella hermitages: in 1053 the monk Desiderio, then Pope Victor III, who built a small church there; Pietro da Morrone found it destroyed in 1246 and started the restoration by adding an oratory and a cell. Today it includes church, sacristy, guesthouse and monastic complex, with wooden choir, paintings of the Madonna and the Descent of the Holy Spirit; under the church the cave of the first hermits, the room of the Crucifix and the cell where Celestine V prayed, and the Santa Scala rises to the oratory of the Maddalena, overlooking the valley. A community of young friars lives there; from August 29th to the first Sunday of October every Sunday forgiveness is celebrated with plenary indulgence.
zcpg18.60: The hermitage-monastery of Celestine V set in the mountain.
hfclfi.701: At about 610 meters below a large rock roof in the Vallone di Santo Spirito, documented from 1275 and rebuilt by Fr.Pietro da Morrone, inhabited still in 1320: the oratory is almost all carved into the rock, with the Holy Staircase on the terrace, two frescoed squares of the thirteenth century on the façade (Madonna with Child and Christ blessing) and, on the sixteenth century altar, the wooden statue of St. Bartholomew; under a stone flows the water considered miraculous. wvh03q.282: The municipality of the hills of Pescia, in whose territory stands Villa Badessa, a community of Arbëreshë arrived from Epirus in 1743: its church of Santa Maria Assunta, unique of Greek-Byzantine rite in Abruzzo, preserves a rich collection of icons, and a museum tells its origins and traditions.
9bopvu.299: The only Greek-Byzantine church in Abruzzo, dependent on the Eparchy of Lungro in Calabria, conserves 75 icons painted on a table from the 15th to the 19th century: for the Ministry it is the main collection of Byzantine and post-Byzantine icons of Western Europe. Visit on request (tel. 388 1655479).
1lu44t2.51: Byzantine icons in an Albanian village in Abruzzo.
1yiflyv.227: It documents the origins of the Albanian community (arbëreshë) of Abruzzo, established here in 1743 by Epirus to escape the religious persecutions of the Turks, and preserves its traditions. Open on request (tel. 338 1655479).
1y3ews9.320: Small hilly town of the Pescarese, in the Val del Fino, with the Museum of Traditions and Rural Arts and a historic centre gathered around Piazza Duca degli Abruzzi and the Baroque church of the Blessed Virgin Mary of the Rescue; in the hamlet of Piccianello rises the neoclassical church of San Rocco (1838).
1ypce2c.258: Museum born from a private initiative that collects objects of everyday rural life, with reconstructions of ancient environments and a late medieval mill recovered in Pacentro; organizes exhibitions on local traditions. Contacts: 085 8285452, info@mutac.org.

iv6vps.514: With Piazza Duca degli Abruzzi it forms the main complex representative of the historic center of Picciano: the monumental brick façade dominates the square, about 130 cm lower than the building, and is divided into three parts by binated pilasters, with central portal between two composite columns under a triangular tympanum and side wings with broken tympanums. The interior, of baroque taste, has an inscribed cross plan, dome on the central compartment and semicircular apse. It is the parish church (fornìa di Penne).

10jm72a.445: Parish church built on a project by Aniello Francia and completed in 1838, on a hill in the middle of the hamlet, in the hilly area of Val del Fino. It has a single rectangular nave marked by Ionian binated pilasters on three spans, with the central covered by a lower dome on plumes; the neoclassical brick façade is crowned by a large triangular tympanum with denticles and has triglyphs in the stripe marchepiano.
